findings.ref: T-009 session notes 'One divergence found and disclosed' (emit-run-record.sh:109-112; .ps1:84-86) vs design.md API/Contract Plan four-row table
findings.note: The implementation rejects --capability-block-id supplied without --capability-enforcement 'regardless of --effort-*', exiting 1 before the table's own row-3 check runs. design.md calls its rows 'The four reachable flag combinations (AC-033) are fixed exhaustively' over exactly two axes, and AC-033 requires each of the four to produce the shape design.md fixes. Under those axes '--effort-main ... --capability-block-id X' IS row 2, whose documented outcome is a successful sdd-run-record/v2 with the effort object only - the implementation exits 1 instead. The claim that this 'does not contradict any row' holds only if the table is read as silent on block-id, which its own 'fixed exhaustively' wording denies. No test in either twin exercises block-id-alone, and the contract's comment confirms it 'is still present and still untested'. A fifth reachable input class with an undocumented, untested fail-closed outcome on a Security Boundary B2 file under Required Workflow tdd is a live contract gap, not a disclosure that can be carried through the gate.

findings.ref: coder-regression.log header: 'Suite list: ... (grep -l emit-run-record tests/*.tests.sh)' and 'Bash only, per that same precedent.'
findings.note: T-009's Planned Files include the PowerShell twin emit-run-record.ps1, yet the required high-tier regression check is Bash-only, and the consumer list was derived from a glob that structurally cannot match a PowerShell suite - so no .ps1 consumer of the modified .ps1 was ever enumerated, let alone executed. All five [RUN] entries are .sh. The stated justification explains skipping run-all; it does not explain skipping the other four consumer suites' .ps1 twins, which were directly invocable - the same session invoked pwsh directly for T-009's own suite. The blast radius of a cross-epic shared surface is verified in one runtime only, with the other runtime's result standing in by assumption.

findings.ref: acceptance-tests.md AC-011 row ('regression, byte-identical | emit-run-record.sh no-flag output unchanged') vs the 50 assertions in the green logs
findings.note: AC-011's designated test was not delivered. No assertion in either twin performs a byte comparison; the entire no-flag coverage is structural. Byte-identity rests solely on verification/T-009/baseline.sha256, which asserts v1_byte_identical=true but - unlike every other evidence log in this bundle, which records '$ <command>' - carries no command line, so the claim cannot be re-derived from the artifact; plus a manual heredoc diff described only in prose. The golden-baseline manifest's nine targets contain no emit-run-record output, so no committed suite locks AC-011 anywhere. traceability.md assigns AC-011/TEST-011 to T-009, making this T-009's obligation. A future whitespace or field-order change to the v1 heredoc would pass the whole 50-assertion suite.

findings.ref: coder-regression.log: 'tests/effort-policy-flip.tests.sh is DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED ... A first pass DID include it and observed exactly one failure'
findings.note: The scope was narrowed after the suite went red, which contradicts the log's own stated selection rule in the same paragraph. The substantive justification is sound and checkable - TEST-046 is an epic-159-pillar-c branch-naming self-check that fails on any branch not named for T-007, and the suite's only emit-run-record call site is skipped without SDD_ALLOW_REAL_CODEX_SMOKE - so no coverage is actually lost and the disclosure is honest. But including the suite with the unrelated failure annotated carries identical information without a scope tailored post-hoc to the observed result.

findings.ref: T-009 decision record ('green.log: Bash and PowerShell each 49 passed') vs session notes ('Bash: 50 passed / 0 failed - green-sh.log')
findings.note: Two contradictory GREEN artifacts remain under verification/T-009/. The session notes reconcile red.log explicitly but never address green.log's 49-vs-50 discrepancy, and the decision record still points at it. A gate reader landing on green.log/red.log rather than green-sh.log/red-sh.log gets stale numbers with nothing marking them superseded.

findings.ref: green/rerun logs: sh 'AC-012 optional block_id: omitted value serializes as null (.capability.block_id = null)' vs ps1 '... ()'
findings.note: design.md fixes the shape as an explicit block_id: null when the flag is not supplied. The exact-key-set assertion is recorded only for the both-flags case; no key-set assertion appears in the omitted-block_id case in either runtime. Since jq's .capability.block_id and PowerShell property access both yield null for an absent key, an emitter that dropped the key entirely would satisfy both logged assertions. This cannot be confirmed either way from the bundle: the suite sources are not included, and the PowerShell parenthetical renders null, empty string, and missing property identically.
